reply:
That changes it: INT is a 32-bit signed integer capped at 2,147,483,647. The 11 in INT(11) is display width for ZEROFILL, not storage limit.

So a 12-digit number overflows not because of the 11, but because INT maxes out at 10 digits. Use BIGINT (64-bit, ~19 digits) if you need 12-digit capacity.

grade.note: Reply correctly adopts developer's explanation that 11 is display width and INT is 32-bit capped at ~2.1 billion.
